# Robinhood Wallet Connector

> **AI agents: start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt).** [Raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Full documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms-full.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

**Connect Robinhood Wallet to mainstream frontend wallet SDKs.**

An open-source integration toolkit for dApp developers, with adapters for **wagmi v2/v3, RainbowKit, and Web3-Onboard**, integrations for **AppKit and ConnectKit** through wagmi, and **ethers v6 and viem** through a framework-independent **EIP-1193 provider**. Additional adapters cover **thirdweb**, **Dynamic React**, and **Privy headless SIWE**. Use it to add a recognizable Robinhood Wallet entry and a dedicated connection dialog to your application.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

A matching injected Robinhood provider is used when available; otherwise, the SDK offers a QR code and an explicit **Open Robinhood Wallet** action through WalletConnect. Each integration includes usage documentation and a runnable example below.

## Packages

| Package | Purpose | Integration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet` | Framework-independent EIP-1193 provider and connection UI | [Core API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi` | wagmi connector | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md) · [v2 example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/wagmi-v2) · [v3 example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/wagmi-v3) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit` | Robinhood entry for `connectorsForWallets` | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/rainbowkit/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/rainbowkit) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard` | Standard Web3-Onboard wallet module | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/web3-onboard/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/onboard) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-thirdweb` | thirdweb Wallet and React hooks | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/thirdweb/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/thirdweb) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-dynamic` | Dynamic custom EVM connector | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/dynamic/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/dynamic) |
| `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-privy` | Privy headless SIWE helper | [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/privy/README.md) · [Example](https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/tree/main/examples/privy) |

The core owns its connection lifecycle and native HTML dialog. It uses `@walletconnect/sign-client` directly and does not depend on AppKit modal internals or patches to a framework wallet chooser. Construction and imports do not request accounts or launch a wallet.

The files are public and can be fetched without a GitHub login. Follow the guide for the framework you use; the documented support matrix and verification limits apply to agent-generated integrations too. When working from a pinned commit, read the documentation from that same commit.

## Install from this repository

These packages have **not been published to npm**. Build and pack the repository, then install the generated tarballs in your application. Node.js 22.12 or newer is required for this development workflow.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
mkdir -p artifacts
npm pack --workspaces --pack-destination artifacts
```

For a standalone provider, install the core tarball:

```sh
npm install /path/to/artifacts/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz
```

Install all required local SDK packages in the **same install command**, so npm can resolve their unpublished dependencies:

| Integration | Required tarballs |
| --- | --- |
| ethers v6 / viem | `vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz` |
| wagmi / AppKit / ConnectKit | `vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz`, `vexi-robinhood-wallet-wagmi-0.1.0.tgz` |
| RainbowKit | Core and wagmi tarballs above, plus `vexi-robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit-0.1.0.tgz` |
| Web3-Onboard | Core tarball, plus `vexi-robinhood-wallet-onboard-0.1.0.tgz` |
| thirdweb / Dynamic / Privy | Core tarball, plus the matching `vexi-robinhood-wallet-thirdweb-0.1.0.tgz`, `vexi-robinhood-wallet-dynamic-0.1.0.tgz` or `vexi-robinhood-wallet-privy-0.1.0.tgz` |

For example, in an existing wagmi v2 application:

```sh
npm install \
  /path/to/artifacts/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz \
  /path/to/artifacts/vexi-robinhood-wallet-wagmi-0.1.0.tgz \
  wagmi@2.19.5 @wagmi/core@2.22.1 viem@2.57.7
```

Use your own WalletConnect project ID and allow the application origin in its project settings. The project ID is browser configuration; the SDK never needs a private key or recovery phrase.

## Use with wagmi

```ts
import { createConfig, http } from 'wagmi';
import { mainnet } from 'wagmi/chains';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi';

export const config = createConfig({
  chains: [mainnet],
  connectors: [robinhoodWallet({
    projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
    metadata: {
      name: 'My app',
      description: 'My app description',
      url: 'https://my-app.example',
      icons: [],
    },
  })],
  transports: { [mainnet.id]: http() },
});
```

Use the resulting connector with wagmi's normal connection hooks or actions. A user selecting **Connect** starts the permission request. The adapter exposes `cancelConnect()` for custom host controls. The runnable examples include the React provider setup.

As with wagmi's built-in connectors, a `chainId` passed to `connect` is a preference: if switching to it fails while the wallet remains connected, the connection stays on the wallet's chain. User rejection, cancellation, disconnection or destruction still rejects the connection attempt. A previously approved session is recovered on reconnect, and by `connect` itself, without a new approval.

## Use with RainbowKit

```ts
import { connectorsForWallets } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit';
import { injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit/wallets';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit';

const connectors = connectorsForWallets([
  { groupName: 'Recommended', wallets: [robinhoodWallet] },
  { groupName: 'Other wallets', wallets: [injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet] },
], {
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  appName: 'My app',
  appUrl: 'https://my-app.example',
});
```

Pass `connectors` to wagmi's `createConfig`. Selecting Robinhood opens the SDK's native modal above the RainbowKit chooser. The underlying page becomes inert while the modal is open; Close or Escape cancels the SDK attempt. After an error, close the dialog and select Robinhood again to start a fresh request. Other wallets remain ordinary RainbowKit entries.

The adapter consumes application metadata from `walletConnectParameters.metadata`; other generic WalletConnect options are not forwarded. RainbowKit can reorder installed and recent wallets according to its own settings.

## Use with Web3-Onboard

```ts
import Onboard from '@web3-onboard/core';
import { robinhoodModule } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard';

const onboard = Onboard({
  wallets: [robinhoodModule({ projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID' })],
  chains: [{
    id: '0x1',
    token: 'ETH',
    label: 'Ethereum',
    rpcUrl: 'https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com',
  }],
  appMetadata: { name: 'My app', description: 'My app description', explore: 'https://my-app.example' },
});

// Call from your Connect button's handler.
async function connectWallet() {
  await onboard.connectWallet();
}
```

Onboard supplies the configured chains, RPC endpoints, and application metadata to the module. Its interface exposes the EIP-1193 provider and the same `RobinhoodProvider` as `instance`. When Onboard reconnects through `eth_requestAccounts`, the provider recovers the previously approved session instead of starting a new pairing.

The tested Onboard dependency tree includes inherited critical and high-severity registry advisories. Review the [dependency notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/dependency-notes.md) before adopting this integration; a passing framework test is not a security certification.

## Use with AppKit, ConnectKit, ethers v6 and viem

These integrations reuse the existing packages, connection dialog and session lifecycle. Each guide includes installation instructions and a runnable application.

| Application | Integration | Guide and example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reown AppKit + React | Pass `robinhoodWallet(options)` to `new WagmiAdapter({ connectors })`, then share `adapter.wagmiConfig` with `WagmiProvider` | [AppKit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/README.md) |
| ConnectKit + React | Include `robinhoodWalletForConnectKit(options)` in the wagmi configuration wrapped by `ConnectKitProvider` | [ConnectKit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/connectkit/README.md) |
| ethers v6, without a React requirement | Wrap the core provider in `new BrowserProvider(provider, 'any')` | [ethers v6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/ethers/README.md) |
| viem, without a React requirement | Use `createWalletClient({ transport: custom(provider, { retryCount: 0 }) })` | [viem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/viem/README.md) |

AppKit and ConnectKit retain their own wallet choosers; the SDK owns Robinhood pairing and cancellation. The direct ethers/viem examples include user-triggered connection, restoration, state events and cleanup. Do not call ethers `getSigner()` or viem `requestAddresses()` during render or a passive account check: they can request permission.

## Use with thirdweb, Dynamic and Privy

| Platform | Public entry point | Integration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| thirdweb | `robinhoodWallet(options)` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-thirdweb` | Standard Wallet with `ThirdwebProvider` and `useConnect`; [guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/thirdweb/README.md) |
| Dynamic React | `robinhoodWalletConnectors(options)` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-dynamic` | Custom connector in `DynamicContextProvider.settings.walletConnectors`; [guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/dynamic/README.md) |
| Privy | `createRobinhoodPrivyLogin(provider, handlers)` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-privy` | Separate connect and sign-in actions using `useLoginWithSiwe`; [guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/privy/README.md) |

These packages reuse the same core discovery, transport, dialog and session behavior. Dynamic uses connect-only mode in its example. Privy uses headless authentication: it does not add a Robinhood entry to Privy's built-in chooser or populate `useWallets()`. The Privy example requests a signature only after **Sign in with Privy** is explicitly selected. Live authentication remains unverified.

## Framework versions

The SDK peer versions and example dependency versions are pinned to the baselines below. The verification record distinguishes completed checks from pending work; these entries are not broad version-range or physical-wallet compatibility claims.

| Integration | Declared baseline |
| --- | --- |
| wagmi v2 | `wagmi 2.19.5`, `@wagmi/core 2.22.1`, `viem 2.57.7` |
| wagmi v3 | `wagmi 3.7.7`, `@wagmi/core 3.6.5`, `viem 2.57.7` |
| RainbowKit | `@rainbow-me/rainbowkit 2.2.11`, wagmi v2 baseline above |
| Web3-Onboard | `@web3-onboard/core 2.24.1`, `@web3-onboard/common 2.4.2` |
| AppKit React + wagmi | `@reown/appkit 1.8.24`, `@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi 1.8.24`, wagmi v3 baseline, React `19.3.1` |
| ConnectKit | `connectkit 1.9.2`, wagmi v2 baseline, React / React DOM `18.3.1` |
| ethers v6 | `ethers 6.17.0`, core SDK only |
| viem | `viem 2.57.7`, core SDK only |
| thirdweb | `thirdweb 5.122.0`, React / React DOM `19.3.1` |
| Dynamic React | `@dynamic-labs/sdk-react-core`, `@dynamic-labs/ethereum-core`, `@dynamic-labs/wallet-connector-core` `5.12.0`, viem `2.57.7`, React `19.3.1` |
| Privy headless SIWE | `@privy-io/react-auth 3.50.0`, viem `2.57.7`, React `19.3.1` |

RainbowKit's listed baseline uses wagmi v2. The separate wagmi v3 example does not establish RainbowKit compatibility with wagmi v3.

ConnectKit's baseline uses React 18 to respect its declared peers. AppKit's fresh dependency resolution requires wagmi core v3; its wagmi v2 combination is not supported by this example. AppKit's other adapters/framework bindings and other ethers/viem versions are outside these checks.

## Connection and verification boundaries

The desktop layout presents a locally generated QR code; narrow viewports use a bottom sheet with the same explicit app-opening action. The SDK does not infer that an app is installed from viewport size. It never signs or sends a transaction automatically. A later application request can ask the connected wallet to approve a supported operation.

The dialog renders inside a shadow root, so the host page's CSS cannot restyle its QR code or controls. In browsers with constructable stylesheets it needs no inline `<style>` element, so it also works under a `style-src 'self'` Content Security Policy; the embedded icon still needs `img-src data:`.

Configured EVM chain IDs are application inputs, not proof of wallet support. Remote sessions must approve the requested chain, account, and method. Robinhood Chain mainnet `4663` and testnet `46630` require separate device and network evidence; neither is certified by this delivery.

Physical Robinhood Wallet pairing, iOS/Android app routing, signatures, and transaction submission remain unverified. Synthetic tests, package builds, and a rendered QR code do not establish those outcomes. See [verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) for recorded evidence and the device checklist.

## Develop and review

```sh
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:all
```

The full suite builds and type-checks all seven SDK packages, runs core and documentation checks, then tests all twelve examples as packed consumers and in desktop/narrow browser viewports. The matrix installs real framework dependencies in isolated temporary applications and uses synthetic wallets. It does not request real wallet approval. Use `BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome npm run test:all` for an installed Chrome browser; see the contributor guide for selected-case commands.

See [architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/architecture.md), [verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md), and [upstream assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/upstream-contributions.md). Package publication, upstream inclusion, deployment, and physical-wallet certification are separate delivery stages.

# Robinhood Wallet integration guide for AI coding agents

Use this guide to add Robinhood Wallet to an existing frontend application. This repository provides a standalone EIP-1193 provider and adapters for wagmi v2/v3, RainbowKit and Web3-Onboard. AppKit and ConnectKit reuse the wagmi connector; ethers v6 and viem wrap the core provider directly. Separate adapters cover thirdweb Wallet, Dynamic React custom connectors and Privy headless SIWE.

Built by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, not an official Robinhood SDK, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

## Choose an integration

Inspect the application's existing wallet framework and dependency versions before choosing a package. Match the exact [supported framework baselines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#framework-versions); do not infer support for other versions or frameworks from shared dependencies.

| Existing application | Public entry point | Guide and runnable source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wagmi v2 | `import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi'` | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v2/README.md), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v2/src/main.tsx) |
| wagmi v3 | Same wagmi entry point | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/wagmi/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v3/README.md), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/wagmi-v3/src/main.tsx) |
| RainbowKit with wagmi v2 | `import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit'` | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/rainbowkit/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/rainbowkit/README.md), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/rainbowkit/src/main.tsx) |
| Web3-Onboard | `import { robinhoodModule } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard'` | [Module guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/web3-onboard/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/onboard/README.md), [app source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/onboard/src/main.ts) |
| AppKit React + wagmi v3 | `robinhoodWallet` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi`, passed to `WagmiAdapter` | [AppKit guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/README.md), [configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/src/config.ts), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/src/main.tsx) |
| ConnectKit + wagmi v2 + React 18 | `robinhoodWalletForConnectKit` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi` | [ConnectKit guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/connectkit/README.md), [configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/connectkit/src/config.ts), [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/connectkit/src/main.tsx) |
| ethers v6 | Core `RobinhoodProvider` wrapped in ethers `BrowserProvider` | [ethers guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/ethers/README.md), [client setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/ethers/src/client.ts), [app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/ethers/src/main.ts) |
| viem | Core `RobinhoodProvider` passed to viem `custom` | [viem guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/viem/README.md), [client setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/viem/src/client.ts), [app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/viem/src/main.ts) |
| thirdweb | `robinhoodWallet` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-thirdweb` | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/thirdweb/README.md), [React example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/thirdweb/README.md) |
| Dynamic React 5.12.0 | `robinhoodWalletConnectors` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-dynamic` | [Adapter guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/dynamic/README.md), [React example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/dynamic/README.md) |
| Privy headless SIWE | `createRobinhoodPrivyLogin` from `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-privy` | [Helper guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/privy/README.md), [React example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/privy/README.md) |
| Vanilla browser or a host that accepts an EIP-1193 provider | `import { RobinhoodProvider } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet'` | [Core API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md), [example setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/README.md), [app source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/main.ts) |

The wagmi, RainbowKit and thirdweb packages all export `robinhoodWallet` with different APIs. The thirdweb factory returns a standard Wallet; for wagmi and RainbowKit: call the wagmi factory with options and put its result in `createConfig({ connectors })`; pass the RainbowKit factory without calling it in a `connectorsForWallets` wallet group. Call `robinhoodModule(options)` for `Onboard({ wallets })`. ConnectKit 1.9.2 needs `robinhoodWalletForConnectKit(options)`: it uses the same provider with the chooser's injected-compatible routing hint, which does not mean an installed wallet was detected. The general `robinhoodWallet` type is displayed as unavailable by that chooser. Keep the application's other wallet entries and provider wrappers intact.

The AppKit example covers its React + wagmi v3 path only. Its broad optional connector dependency currently resolves to a release requiring wagmi core v3; the wagmi v2 combination failed a fresh build. ConnectKit uses React 18 and wagmi v2 to match its declared peers. No separate AppKit, ConnectKit, ethers or viem SDK package is needed. AppKit's other framework bindings/adapters remain outside the verified integrations. thirdweb uses a custom connection button and active-wallet hooks. Dynamic targets its React 5.12.0 SDK, not its newer JavaScript SDK. Privy uses `useLoginWithSiwe` after an independent core connection; its built-in chooser and `useWallets()` do not receive this wallet. RainbowKit uses the documented wagmi v2 baseline; the separate wagmi v3 example does not extend that claim.

## Install the actual packages

The packages are **unpublished**. Do not suggest installing these `@vexi` package names directly from the npm registry. With Node.js 22.12 or newer, prepare tarballs from a checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector.git
cd robinhood-wallet-connector
npm ci
npm run build
mkdir -p artifacts
npm pack --workspaces --pack-destination artifacts
```

In the consuming application, install the required tarballs together in one `npm install` command so npm can resolve their unpublished dependencies:

| Integration | Local SDK packages required |
| --- | --- |
| Core / ethers v6 / viem | `@vexi/robinhood-wallet` |
| wagmi / AppKit / ConnectKit | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi` |
| RainbowKit | Core + wagmi adapter + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit` |
| Web3-Onboard | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard` |
| thirdweb | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-thirdweb` |
| Dynamic React | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-dynamic` |
| Privy headless SIWE | Core + `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-privy` |

Use the exact tarball filenames and installation example in the [installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository), and install the chosen framework's declared peer dependencies. The examples' `package.json` files provide working dependency sets. The packages expose ESM and TypeScript declarations; use public `import` entry points, not CommonJS `require` or files from `src`, `dist` or the internal modal implementation.

## Configure the host application

1. Supply your own WalletConnect `projectId` and allow the application's actual origin in that project's settings. In the Vite examples, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, set `VITE_WC_PROJECT_ID`, and restart the development server. The ID is public application configuration; no wallet private key or recovery phrase belongs here.
2. Provide application metadata with a name, description, absolute HTTP(S) URL and icon array. For RainbowKit, pass `appName` and `appUrl` to `connectorsForWallets`. For Onboard, supply `appMetadata` or explicit module `metadata`.
3. Configure the EVM chain IDs and usable RPC endpoints. Core takes numeric `chains` and `rpcMap`; wagmi derives them from its configured chains with an optional `rpcMap` override; Onboard derives them from its chain entries, which use hexadecimal IDs such as `0x1`. Use the existing application chain setup when appropriate.
4. Create a stable provider or connector configuration rather than creating another instance on every render. If independent core/wagmi/Onboard instances need separate persisted sessions, give them distinct, stable `storagePrefix` values.
5. For thirdweb, Dynamic or Privy, also supply the platform's own client/environment/app ID. Use the pinned peers in its guide. Dynamic's enabled networks must match the core configuration; its declarations require bundler module resolution. Privy requires wallet authentication enabled in the dashboard.
6. Start connection only from the user's Connect action, using the framework's normal connection API or `provider.connect()`. Display pending, cancellation and error states; prevent repeated host clicks while pending. Connecting does not automatically sign or send transactions.

Imports and core construction are safe without `window`, but interactive wallet use requires a browser. Supply metadata URLs explicitly for server rendering; the runnable Vite examples use `window.location.origin` and need adaptation before copying into server-executed code. Keep the consuming framework's own client/server boundaries intact.

The default UI requires native `HTMLDialogElement.showModal()` and Shadow DOM. It renders in a shadow root under one `<rhw-connector>` element, so the host page's CSS does not restyle it. Where constructable stylesheets are supported, it needs no inline `<style>` element, so a `style-src 'self'` Content Security Policy works; the embedded icon still needs `img-src data:`. See the [core UI requirements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md#discovery-and-session-scope) if the host needs a custom UI.

## Preserve the connection lifecycle

| Host action or condition | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Connect | Use the chosen adapter or `provider.connect({ chainId })`. A previously approved, persisted session is recovered first, without a new approval. Otherwise a matching Robinhood injected provider is preferred, and failing that the SDK pairs through WalletConnect with its dedicated Robinhood dialog. Core `connect({ chainId })` requires that chain; the wagmi and RainbowKit adapters treat a requested chain as a preference, as wagmi's built-in connectors do. A failed preferred switch can fall back only while the same connection remains active; user rejection, cancellation, disconnection or destruction still rejects the connection attempt. |
| Cancel pending connection | Close the SDK dialog or press Escape. Custom controls can call `provider.cancel()` or the wagmi connector's `cancelConnect()`. Core cancellation rejects with code `4001`; wagmi maps it to its normal user-rejection error. A wallet rejection that WalletConnect reports as `USER_REJECTED` also arrives as `4001`. The connection promise settles even if saved-session recovery is waiting on a stalled wallet response. Cancellation does not revoke an established connection, interrupt its requests, or dismiss an injected wallet's own permission prompt. In particular, `cancelConnect()` during the adapter's preferred-chain switch rejects the unfinished adapter attempt but keeps the already-approved core session; use `disconnect()` to clear that session. |
| Retry after rejection, cancellation or error | Settle the old host request, close any error dialog, and start a fresh request from a new user action. Do not automatically reopen permission prompts. Core shares matching concurrent attempts; the wagmi adapter shares a repeated pending connect and rejects one for a different chain with `ResourceUnavailableRpcError`. |
| Recover after reload | Use the framework's reconnect flow, `provider.isAuthorized()`, or an explicit Connect. Recovery checks previously approved state without requesting account permission and may initialize remote transport; it keeps the session's approved chain and account selection, and revokes a session that approves none of the configured chains. `eth_accounts` alone only reads the current instance's cache. |
| Account or chain changes | Use the framework's reactive state. With core, subscribe to `accountsChanged`, `chainChanged` and `disconnect`; update application state and remove listeners on disposal. An empty account list means access is gone. |
| Disconnect | Use the framework's disconnect API or `provider.disconnect()`. This clears local state and disconnects this transport's approved remote session and its pairing. Wallet-side revocation is best effort: the promise resolves after local cleanup even when the wallet cannot be reached. It does not revoke injected-wallet permissions. |
| Dispose a core instance | `provider.destroy()` releases its UI and listeners while preserving an approved persisted session for recovery by a later instance. It is not a logout action; the destroyed instance cannot reconnect. |

Core `connect()` returns a numeric `chainId`; EIP-1193 `chainChanged` and `eth_chainId` use hexadecimal strings. Before connection, the core `getChainId()` reflects the configured initial chain, not wallet approval; the wagmi connector's `getChainId()` reports an in-app Robinhood wallet's current chain when one is present, read with `eth_chainId` and no permission request. See the [core API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md#api) for complete methods, events and session semantics.

## Avoid common integration mistakes

- **One pairing UI:** leave the SDK's dialog enabled when using the supplied adapters. RainbowKit, AppKit and ConnectKit provide host choosers; the SDK owns Robinhood's remote pairing dialog. Do not add another QR handler for this connector or use AppKit `customWallets` as a substitute for installing the connector.
- **One wagmi config:** AppKit's React provider must receive `adapter.wagmiConfig`; ConnectKit consumes its surrounding `WagmiProvider` configuration. Preserve other wallet entries. Do not mix the two different wagmi baselines or assume ConnectKit supports React 19.
- **Generic wallet restoration:** the RainbowKit example keeps its Browser Wallet entry on a targetless wagmi connector, so it restores only its own explicit connection. A generic connector targeting the same injected provider can otherwise restore Robinhood's approval as a second connection. Verify that disconnect does not leave such a duplicate active; see the [example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/rainbowkit/README.md).
- **Direct clients:** ethers `getSigner()` and viem `requestAddresses()` can request account permission. Use them only after explicit intent. Read accounts passively with `listAccounts()` / `getAddresses()` and restore through core `isAuthorized()`. Use `custom(provider, { retryCount: 0 })`; clear cached signer/account selections on events and disconnect. Subscribe to EIP-1193 events on the core provider and remove listeners on disposal. An ethers wrapper's `destroy()` does not disconnect the SDK session.
- **Authentication requires separate intent:** Dynamic's example uses connect-only mode. Privy's helper must be called only from an explicit sign-in action; `login()` requests a signature and does not connect the wallet. Cancel stale flows on account/chain changes and teardown. A submitted login cannot be withdrawn; late completion is signed out. Keep wallet disconnect and application logout policies explicit.
- **Custom UI is a complete responsibility:** for integrations exposing `showModal: false`, subscribe to `display_uri` before connecting, provide QR/link rendering and cancellation, and clear sensitive pairing data after cancellation or completion. Import `getRobinhoodUri` from the core to construct the app link, and open it only on an explicit click. Follow the [custom UI contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/core/README.md#custom-connection-ui).
- **Wallet identity:** discovery uses `com.robinhood.wallet` EIP-6963 metadata or `isRobinhoodMobileWallet`. Do not rename an arbitrary injected provider or a generic WalletConnect connector to Robinhood. These identity hints are not cryptographic vendor authentication.
- **Network approval:** adding a chain ID does not establish wallet support. A remote session must approve the requested chain, accounts and methods. Switching between chains the session approved is local and shows no wallet prompt; a chain the session did not approve is rejected with `4901`. Robinhood Chain mainnet `4663` and testnet `46630` each need their own device/network evidence.
- **Sensitive data:** keep pairing URIs, session keys and wallet account information out of analytics, logs, screenshots and error reports. A public WalletConnect project ID does not make pairing material public.
- **Dependency risk:** read the [dependency notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/dependency-notes.md), especially for the documented inherited Onboard advisories. Passing integration tests is not a security audit.

## Verify and describe the result

Use the selected example to verify the normal framework flow and run the consuming application's build and type checks. For changes to this repository, follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). `npm run test:all` runs the SDK/core/documentation checks and all twelve packed/browser cases: `vanilla`, `wagmi-v2`, `wagmi-v3`, `rainbowkit`, `onboard`, `appkit`, `connectkit`, `ethers`, `viem`, `thirdweb`, `dynamic` and `privy`. Install Playwright Chromium first, or set `BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome`. The Vanilla and Onboard examples require explicit reconnection after reload; other examples restore saved approval. Neither behavior may request account permission on page load.

Check user-triggered connection, cancellation, retry, pending-state cleanup, disconnect, restored sessions, account/chain events and other wallet entries. UI work also needs desktop/narrow-viewport, keyboard and focus checks. The [vanilla fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/vanilla/fixture.ts) offers a synthetic transport for repeatable UI checks; its QR cannot pair a real wallet.

Report the exact framework versions and checks performed. Keep synthetic tests, browser relay checks and physical-wallet results separate. Physical iOS/Android pairing, app routing, signatures and transaction submission remain unverified in the [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md); do not present a rendered QR or a successful build as proof of them. Real wallet approval and signing belong to a separately authorized manual test.

# Source: packages/core/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet provider

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

`@vexi/robinhood-wallet` provides a framework-independent EIP-1193 provider and a dedicated Robinhood Wallet connection dialog for frontend applications. It is the shared core behind this toolkit's wagmi, RainbowKit, Web3-Onboard, thirdweb and Dynamic adapters, and its Privy headless SIWE helper. AppKit and ConnectKit reuse wagmi; ethers and viem consume the provider directly.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

This package is currently unpublished. Build the repository and install `vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz` generated by `npm pack`; see the [repository installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository). ESM and TypeScript declarations are included. Node.js 22.12 or newer is the development baseline; wallet interaction runs in the browser.

## Minimal browser usage

```ts
import { RobinhoodProvider } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet';

const provider = new RobinhoodProvider({
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  chains: [1],
  rpcMap: { 1: 'https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com' },
  metadata: {
    name: 'My app',
    description: 'My app description',
    url: 'https://my-app.example',
    icons: [],
  },
});

// Wire these functions to user controls in your application.
async function connectWallet() {
  try {
    const { accounts, chainId } = await provider.connect({ chainId: 1 });
    return { accounts, chainId };
  } catch {
    // Present a local error or retry control. Do not log pairing material.
    return undefined;
  }
}

async function disconnectWallet() {
  await provider.disconnect();
}
```

Constructing the provider does not request accounts, initialize the remote transport, or open a dialog. Invoke `connect()` or `eth_requestAccounts` only after the user chooses to connect. A real WalletConnect project ID with the application's origin allowed is required for remote pairing.

## Direct ethers and viem clients

Use this package directly with ethers **6.17.0** or viem **2.57.7**; neither integration requires wagmi or an additional adapter package. The [ethers example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/ethers/README.md) wraps it in `BrowserProvider`. The [viem example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/viem/README.md) uses `custom(provider, { retryCount: 0 })`. Both include cancellation, non-prompting recovery, account/chain events and teardown. EIP-1193 events remain on this core provider, and disposing a client wrapper does not log out of the SDK session.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `projectId: string` | WalletConnect project ID used when remote transport is needed. |
| `chains: readonly number[]` | Nonempty list of configured EVM chain IDs. The first initializes the local chain value. |
| `optionalChains?: readonly number[]` | Additional configured EVM chain IDs offered to the wallet. |
| `rpcMap?: Record<number, string>` | RPC endpoints used for supported read requests through the remote provider. |
| `metadata` | Application `{ name, description, url, icons }`. Supply an HTTP(S) application URL. |
| `showModal?: boolean` | Defaults to `true`. Set `false` only when the host handles connection links and cancellation. |
| `connectTimeoutMs?: number` | Timeout for a connection attempt, including its wait for saved-session recovery, default `120000`. |
| `discoveryTimeoutMs?: number` | Injected-provider discovery window, default `200`. |
| `storagePrefix?: string` | Isolates this connector's persisted session state; defaults to a project-ID-based prefix. |

Both chain arrays form the offered remote namespace. They are not a claim that Robinhood supports all entries, and approval of every configured chain is not required. `connect({ chainId })` requires approval of that specific configured chain. Remote operations also require the relevant session permission.

Give distinct independent connector instances distinct stable `storagePrefix` values. Reusing a prefix intentionally shares the persisted session namespace. Keep the prefix stable across reloads when session recovery is desired.

## API

| API | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `connect({ chainId? }?)` | Returns `{ accounts: string[], chainId: number }`. First recovers this connector's previously approved, persisted session without a new approval request. Otherwise opens the remote dialog if no matching injected provider is found. |
| `request({ method, params? })` | EIP-1193 request. `eth_requestAccounts` starts connection, with the same session recovery as `connect()`; `eth_accounts` reads the local cache; `eth_chainId` returns a hexadecimal chain ID. Other requests require a connection. |
| `cancel()` | Cancels a pending attempt, or the session recovery that `connect()` is waiting on, and closes its dialog. Does not disconnect an established connection or interrupt its requests. |
| `disconnect()` | Cancels pending work, clears local account/session selection, and disconnects this transport's approved remote session and its pairing. Injected wallet permissions are not revoked. Wallet-side revocation is best effort: when the wallet cannot be reached, local state is still cleared and the promise resolves. |
| `destroy()` | Releases this provider's UI and listeners. Preserves an approved persisted session for a later provider instance; does not revoke it. The destroyed instance cannot reconnect. |
| `isAuthorized()` | Attempts to recover this connector's previously approved session without requesting account permission. Returns `boolean`; may initialize remote transport to inspect saved state. |
| `getAccounts()` | Returns a copy of the current cached accounts, or an empty list before connection/recovery. |
| `getChainId()` | Returns the local numeric chain ID. Before connection, this is the first configured chain, not a wallet confirmation. |
| `status` | `idle`, `connecting`, or `connected`. |
| `transport` | `injected`, `walletConnect`, or `undefined`. |
| `connected` | Whether this instance has adopted a connection. |
| `on(event, listener)` / `removeListener(event, listener)` | Subscribe to or remove a provider event listener. |

No connection method automatically requests a signature or submits a transaction. The generic `request()` API can forward signing or transaction methods only when an application explicitly requests them and the connected wallet/session supports them. Wallet approval and rejection remain wallet decisions.

### Events

The provider emits `connect` with `{ chainId: string }`, `accountsChanged` with an account array, `chainChanged` with a hexadecimal string, `disconnect`, and forwarded `message` events. Remote pairing emits `display_uri` with sensitive WalletConnect pairing material.

Keep connection state current through events instead of assuming a connection remains valid indefinitely. Remove your listeners when the host component is disposed. A changed chain or empty account list must be handled by the host application.

Events report actual changes: a chain switch or session update that leaves the account list unchanged does not emit `accountsChanged`. When the wallet removes every account, the provider emits one empty `accountsChanged` and then `disconnect`, even if a listener disconnects in between. A listener that throws is reported through the platform `reportError()` where available, as `EventTarget` does, and never interrupts the provider.

### Retry and cancellation

Matching concurrent core connection requests share the current attempt; a conflicting requested chain is rejected. Closing the SDK dialog or pressing Escape rejects the pending attempt with code `4001`. Saved-session recovery also has a bounded, cancellable wait: cancelling, disconnecting or destroying the provider settles the waiting connection without waiting for a stalled wallet response. The same timeout and cancellation cover a requested-chain switch during recovery. A timeout also terminates the wait or attempt; late recovery results cannot adopt a connection or clear a newer recovery. Late remote approval is cleaned up for its original session topic instead of adopting it after cancellation.

A wallet that rejects the connection proposal or a request with WalletConnect's `USER_REJECTED` codes (`5000`–`5003`) is reported with EIP-1193 code `4001`; the original WalletConnect error is kept as `data`.

The default error view keeps a Close action and explains how to retry from the application. Call `connect()` again from a new host action to create a fresh request. The framework adapters retain their framework's normal error and connection state.

### Custom connection UI

With `showModal: false`, subscribe to `display_uri` before connecting and handle the link in your own UI. Use exported `getRobinhoodUri(uri)` to validate a WalletConnect v2 URI and construct the `robinhood-wallet://wc?uri=...` app link. Launch that link only after an explicit user action.

Your UI must offer cancellation through `provider.cancel()`, clear its QR/link on close and completion, and ignore results from an obsolete attempt. Do not send pairing URIs to QR services, analytics, logs, or error-reporting systems. The default modal generates its QR in the browser and clears the URI and canvas when closed.

`ConnectionModal` and `ProviderDependencies` describe the internal host/test seams. `RobinhoodModal` is an implementation detail, not a public package export.

## Discovery and session scope

Discovery checks the published `com.robinhood.wallet` EIP-6963 identity and the `isRobinhoodMobileWallet` injected-provider flag. It does not select an arbitrary `window.ethereum` provider and change its label. These hints distinguish compatible provider advertisements; they are not cryptographic vendor authentication.

Remote connections use `@walletconnect/sign-client` **2.26.0**. The core owns its approved session topic and requests only within its authorized EVM namespace. Read calls use the corresponding configured `rpcMap` endpoint. The SDK uses browser persistence where available, while WalletConnect maintains its own session/key storage. Providers that share a storage prefix share one SignClient per page, created with the first provider's project ID and metadata, because WalletConnect keeps one Core per prefix; a provider created after `destroy()` reuses it.

A restored session is validated for expiry and approved accounts/chains before adoption. It keeps the saved chain and account selection while the session still approves them; if the saved chain is no longer configured, it uses another configured chain the session approved. A session that approves none of the configured chains is revoked rather than left approved.

Switching between chains the session already approved is local, as in WalletConnect's `UniversalProvider`: every request names its chain, so the wallet is not prompted. A chain the session did not approve is rejected with `4901`. Session events may encode chains as numbers, hexadecimal or decimal strings, or CAIP-2 IDs, and accounts as addresses or CAIP-10 IDs; the decoded values are still checked against the session's approval. A wallet's session extension is honored.

Imports and construction are safe without a browser. Interactive use requires a browser; the default modal requires native `HTMLDialogElement.showModal()` and Shadow DOM. The dialog renders in a shadow root under a single `<rhw-connector>` element, so host page CSS does not restyle it. Where constructable stylesheets are supported, its CSS is applied without an inline `<style>` element, so a `style-src 'self'` Content Security Policy works; other browsers fall back to an inline style element. The icon is an embedded data URL, so the policy must still allow `img-src data:`, or the application should supply its own UI.

## Verification and licensing

Framework builds, synthetic lifecycle tests, real browser checks, and physical-wallet tests are separate evidence. Actual iOS/Android pairing, signatures, transaction submission, and Robinhood Chain `4663`/`46630` support remain unverified. Configuring a chain does not certify it. Consult the repository's [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) for the current evidence scope.

Code is MIT-licensed. Third-party names and branding are not relicensed under MIT and do not imply endorsement. The embedded Robinhood icon is attributed to the [Robinhood Wallet App Store listing, ID 1634080733](https://apps.apple.com/app/id1634080733); its PNG SHA-256 is `8036938af96b8d0a7fec88c8bdb8e5fbc1ef59e7759b55d5d59667f7513fa951`.

# Robinhood Wallet for wagmi

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

Connect Robinhood Wallet to wagmi v2/v3 using the toolkit's provider and dedicated connection dialog.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

These packages are not published to npm. Follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository) before using this adapter.

```ts
import { createConfig, http } from 'wagmi';
import { mainnet } from 'wagmi/chains';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi';

export const config = createConfig({
  chains: [mainnet],
  connectors: [robinhoodWallet({
    projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
    metadata: {
      name: 'My app',
      description: 'My app description',
      url: 'https://my-app.example',
      icons: [],
    },
  })],
  transports: { [mainnet.id]: http() },
});
```

Use wagmi's normal `useConnect`, `useDisconnect`, and wallet client APIs. Connection requests start only after an explicit connect action. A discovered Robinhood provider is selected by its published identity hints; other injected providers are never relabeled. Without one, the SDK opens a dedicated Robinhood dialog using WalletConnect as transport.

`getProvider()` returns the stable `RobinhoodProvider`. `cancelConnect()` rejects an unfinished adapter connection, including its preferred-chain switch. If wallet approval has already completed, the core session and any wallet-side request remain active; use `disconnect()` to clear the session. `disconnect()` clears the connector's session and listeners; it does not revoke permissions in another wallet or modify another connector's session. Chain switching requires a configured chain and the applicable wallet or session approval; switching between already-approved WalletConnect chains is local. The chain list is application configuration, not evidence that Robinhood supports every configured network.

As with wagmi's built-in `injected` and `walletConnect` connectors, a `chainId` passed to `connect` is a preference. After the wallet approves, the connector asks to switch; if the switch fails while the wallet remains connected, the connection stays on the wallet's current chain. User rejection, cancellation, disconnection or destruction still rejects the connection attempt; it cannot return a successful connection with an empty account list. Before connecting, `getChainId()` reports an in-app Robinhood wallet's current chain (read with `eth_chainId`, which needs no account permission), so hosts such as RainbowKit do not request a needless switch. Without one, it reports the first configured chain. A repeated `connect` while one is pending shares that request; one for a different chain fails with `ResourceUnavailableRpcError`.

Compatibility baselines: wagmi **2.19.5** / `@wagmi/core` **2.22.1**, or wagmi **3.7.7** / `@wagmi/core` **3.6.5**, with Viem **2.57.7**. The repository matrix validates packed packages against both. Runnable examples are in `examples/wagmi-v2` and `examples/wagmi-v3`.

Use `showModal: false` only if your host handles `display_uri` and exposes cancellation. `isAuthorized()` and reconnection never request account permission. SSR import is supported; wallet interaction requires a browser.

## AppKit and ConnectKit

The same provider and lifecycle power the pinned [AppKit React + wagmi v3 example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/README.md) and [ConnectKit + wagmi v2 / React 18 example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/connectkit/README.md). Pass `robinhoodWallet(options)` to AppKit's `WagmiAdapter` connectors. Use the named export **`robinhoodWalletForConnectKit(options)`** in the wagmi config consumed by `ConnectKitProvider`. It takes the same `RobinhoodWalletParameters` and preserves `getProvider()` and `cancelConnect()`. These integrations add examples and packed-consumer verification, with no new SDK package or connection implementation. ConnectKit 1.9.2 requires `type: 'injected'` to route this SDK connector through its EIP-1193 screen; the helper changes only that routing field. This does not detect an installed wallet or select an arbitrary injected provider. The normal `robinhoodWallet` type is not actionable in that chooser. Keep the SDK dialog enabled, retain other wallet entries, and follow each guide's exact dependency baseline.

# Robinhood Wallet for RainbowKit

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

Add a Robinhood Wallet entry to RainbowKit with the toolkit's dedicated connection dialog.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

These packages are not published to npm. Follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository) before using this adapter.

Add Robinhood first in your wallet list:

```ts
import { connectorsForWallets } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit';
import { injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet } from '@rainbow-me/rainbowkit/wallets';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-rainbowkit';

const connectors = connectorsForWallets([
  { groupName: 'Recommended', wallets: [robinhoodWallet] },
  { groupName: 'Other wallets', wallets: [injectedWallet, walletConnectWallet] },
], {
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  appName: 'My app',
  appUrl: 'https://my-app.example',
});
```

Pass `connectors` to wagmi's `createConfig`, then use the ordinary `WagmiProvider`, `QueryClientProvider`, `RainbowKitProvider`, and `ConnectButton`. The complete runnable app is in `examples/rainbowkit`.

This adapter targets **RainbowKit 2.2.11 + wagmi 2.19.5**. RainbowKit currently declares a wagmi v2 peer; the separate wagmi adapter supports the tested v3 baseline, but that does not imply RainbowKit v3 compatibility.

Selecting Robinhood opens the SDK's native top-layer dialog, with its own close, Escape, and app-opening controls. Close it and select Robinhood again to retry. The underlying wallet chooser remains inert until the SDK dialog closes. This deliberately omits RainbowKit's `qrCode` and `mobile` hooks: RainbowKit's native Back navigation has no public cancellation callback for a pending wallet proposal. A second pairing modal or a private controller patch is unnecessary.

RainbowKit always passes a chain to wagmi's `connect`. The wagmi adapter treats it as a preference, as wagmi's built-in connectors do: if the wallet session does not approve that chain, or the in-app wallet cannot switch to it, the connection stays on the wallet's chain instead of failing. User rejection, cancellation, disconnection or destruction still rejects the connection attempt; a lost connection is never converted into a successful empty-account result.

The adapter consumes `walletConnectParameters.metadata` generated by `connectorsForWallets`. Other generic WalletConnect provider options are not forwarded: this package owns its session transport and lifecycle. Configuration order controls the recommended group; RainbowKit may show installed or recent wallets before it according to its own settings.

For server-rendered applications, always supply an absolute HTTP(S) `appUrl` to `connectorsForWallets` as shown above. The direct `robinhoodWallet` factory also accepts `appUrl` and `appDescription`, or an explicit `walletConnectParameters.metadata` object. This lets `createConfig`, `getProvider`, and `isAuthorized` run without `window` and without requesting accounts. Browser-only applications may omit the URL to use the current origin; a factory created on the server without a URL cannot initialize a provider until a valid URL is supplied.

A displayed QR code is not proof of physical-wallet approval or network support.

---

# Source: packages/web3-onboard/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/web3-onboard/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet for Web3-Onboard

> **AI integration docs:** [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

A Robinhood Wallet module for Web3-Onboard with the toolkit's dedicated connection dialog. Web3-Onboard originated at Blocknative and is now maintained at `thirdweb-dev/web3-onboard`.

Built and maintained by **[Vexi Lab](https://vexi-protocol.ai) (an onchain options protocol)**. This is an independent community project, **not an official Robinhood SDK**, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Robinhood.

These packages are not published to npm. Follow the [tarball installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository) before using this adapter.

```ts
import Onboard from '@web3-onboard/core';
import { robinhoodModule } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-onboard';

const onboard = Onboard({
  wallets: [robinhoodModule({ projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID' })],
  chains: [{
    id: '0x1',
    label: 'Ethereum',
    token: 'ETH',
    rpcUrl: 'https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com',
  }],
  appMetadata: { name: 'My app', description: 'My app description', explore: 'https://my-app.example' },
});

// Invoke from a user's Connect button.
const wallets = await onboard.connectWallet();
```

The module derives chain IDs and RPC URLs from Onboard's configured chains. Metadata defaults to `appMetadata`, or can be supplied explicitly to `robinhoodModule`. `getInterface` returns a stable EIP-1193 `provider` and exposes the same `RobinhoodProvider` as `instance`; it does not request accounts until Onboard calls `eth_requestAccounts`.

Robinhood's dedicated native dialog owns remote pairing cancellation. Close it and select Robinhood again to retry. A matching injected Robinhood provider is used when present. Other wallet modules remain independent. Supply a public WalletConnect project ID with the app origin allowed in its dashboard; never supply a private key or recovery phrase.

Onboard reconnects through `eth_requestAccounts`, including with `connect.autoConnectLastWallet`. The provider first recovers the session the user approved earlier, so a reload does not open a new pairing or leave the old session behind. If that session has expired or been removed, the request opens a new pairing dialog, including during an automatic reconnect. A wallet rejection is reported with code `4001`, which Onboard shows as a rejected connection with its retry action.

Compatibility baseline: `@web3-onboard/core` **2.24.1**, `@web3-onboard/common` **2.4.2**. See the standalone app in `examples/onboard` and the packed-package framework matrix.

Configuring a network does not establish wallet support for it. No transaction is sent automatically.

---

# Source: packages/thirdweb/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/thirdweb/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet for thirdweb

> **AI agents: start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt).** [Raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

An independent community adapter for `thirdweb 5.122.0`. It implements thirdweb's public `Wallet` interface and delegates discovery, permission requests, WalletConnect, cancellation and persistence to the core provider. This package is unpublished and is not endorsed by Robinhood or thirdweb.

## Install

Build and pack the repository as described in the [root guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository), then install both tarballs together:

```sh
npm install /path/to/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz \
  /path/to/vexi-robinhood-wallet-thirdweb-0.1.0.tgz thirdweb@5.122.0
```

## Use

```ts
import { createThirdwebClient } from 'thirdweb';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-thirdweb';

const client = createThirdwebClient({ clientId: 'YOUR_THIRDWEB_CLIENT_ID' });
const wallet = robinhoodWallet({
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID',
  chains: [1],
  metadata: { name: 'My app', description: 'My app', url: 'https://app.example', icons: [] },
});

// Only from a user-initiated connection action:
await wallet.connect({ client });
const account = wallet.getAccount();
```

Within `ThirdwebProvider`, use `useConnect().connect(async () => { await wallet.connect({ client }); return wallet; })` to populate thirdweb's active wallet hooks. The [React example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/thirdweb/README.md) also restores saved approval with `wallet.autoConnect()` and `useSetActiveWallet`. This delivery uses a custom connection button; thirdweb's built-in wallet chooser is not part of the verified surface.

## Lifecycle

- `connect({ client, chain? })` requests permission through the core; construction does not.
- `autoConnect({ client, chain? })` restores only previously approved state. It rejects if no saved connection exists and does not request accounts or switch chains.
- `cancelConnect()` cancels a pending connection. A late injected approval is ignored; it cannot dismiss a wallet-owned prompt.
- `disconnect()` clears the SDK session and framework listeners. Use thirdweb's `useDisconnect` when the wallet is active in its React context.
- `destroy()` releases resources while retaining the core's persisted approval for another instance. Do not reuse a destroyed wallet.
- `getProvider()` exposes the same `RobinhoodProvider`. `subscribe` follows thirdweb's account, chain, connection and disconnect events; unsubscribe when disposing consumers.

The adapter uses [`EIP1193.fromProvider`](https://portal.thirdweb.com/typescript/v5/adapters) for account operations after the core has connected. It deliberately uses thirdweb's passive adoption path to avoid automatic permission retries. A new internal adapter is created after each disconnect so chain subscriptions survive reconnect. The core owns session disconnect; thirdweb's experimental permission revocation is not forwarded. Normal thirdweb client service and telemetry behavior still applies.

See [verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) for the exact checks and limits. No physical wallet, real signature, transaction, smart account, React Native or other thirdweb version is certified by these checks.

---

# Source: packages/dynamic/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/dynamic/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet for Dynamic

> **AI agents: start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt).** [Raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

A custom EVM wallet connector for Dynamic's React SDK `5.12.0`. It extends the public `EthereumWalletConnector` from `@dynamic-labs/ethereum-core` and uses the core Robinhood provider for discovery, WalletConnect and connection lifecycle. This is an unpublished community package without Robinhood or Dynamic endorsement.

## Install

Follow the [build and pack guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository), then install both SDK tarballs and the pinned peers:

```sh
npm install /path/to/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz \
  /path/to/vexi-robinhood-wallet-dynamic-0.1.0.tgz \
  @dynamic-labs/sdk-react-core@5.12.0 @dynamic-labs/ethereum-core@5.12.0 \
  @dynamic-labs/wallet-connector-core@5.12.0 viem@2.57.7
```

The Dynamic declarations use extensionless re-exports. Use TypeScript's `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` for this integration, as in the runnable example.

## Register the connector

```tsx
import { DynamicContextProvider, DynamicWidget } from '@dynamic-labs/sdk-react-core';
import { robinhoodWalletConnectors } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-dynamic';

const RobinhoodConnectors = robinhoodWalletConnectors({
  projectId: 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID', chains: [1],
  metadata: { name: 'My app', description: 'My app', url: 'https://app.example', icons: [] },
});

function App() {
  return <DynamicContextProvider settings={{
    environmentId: 'YOUR_DYNAMIC_ENVIRONMENT_ID',
    initialAuthenticationMode: 'connect-only',
    walletConnectors: [RobinhoodConnectors],
  }}><DynamicWidget/></DynamicContextProvider>;
}
```

Configure the same enabled EVM networks in Dynamic and the Robinhood options. The factory does not modify other connectors; include it alongside existing connector factories. Do not add a second Robinhood connector under the same key.

`getAddress()` / `connect()` are permission-bearing actions. `getConnectedAccounts()` only restores approved state; `init()` announces readiness without creating a transport. The connector exposes `provider`, `cancelConnect()` and `destroy()` for custom hosts. `endSession()` disconnects and clears listeners. Repeated setup/teardown is supported, and account/chain/disconnect events are translated to Dynamic events. viem wallet clients use `retryCount: 0`.

Dynamic calls its custom SDK routing flag `canConnectViaCustodialService`; the adapter sets that flag to make its own connection UI reachable. This is a framework routing convention, not a claim that Robinhood is custodial or that its mobile app is installed. Provider identity is still checked by the core.

See the [runnable example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/dynamic/README.md), [upstream custom connector guide](https://github.com/dynamic-labs/public-wallet-connectors/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md). The example uses connect-only mode. Dynamic authentication, embedded wallets, the newer JavaScript SDK, physical devices and actual signing are outside the verified surface.

---

# Source: packages/privy/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/packages/privy/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet with Privy headless SIWE

> **AI agents: start with [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt).** [Raw text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/llms.txt) · [Integration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/ai-integration.md)

An unpublished community helper for `@privy-io/react-auth 3.50.0` and `viem 2.57.7`. It connects an already-approved Robinhood provider to Privy's public [`useLoginWithSiwe`](https://docs.privy.io/authentication/user-authentication/login-methods/wallet) flow. It does not add an entry to Privy's built-in wallet chooser or populate `useWallets()`. Robinhood and Privy do not endorse this package.

## Install

Follow the [build and pack guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository), then install both tarballs together:

```sh
npm install /path/to/vexi-robinhood-wallet-0.1.0.tgz \
  /path/to/vexi-robinhood-wallet-privy-0.1.0.tgz \
  @privy-io/react-auth@3.50.0 viem@2.57.7
```

Enable wallet authentication and configure allowed origins in your own Privy application. A Privy app ID and a WalletConnect project ID are separate public identifiers. Neither requires a server secret in the browser.

## Use

Create one `RobinhoodProvider` for the application and connect it from a user action. Inside `PrivyProvider`, pass the methods from `useLoginWithSiwe()` and `usePrivy()` to the helper:

```ts
import { createRobinhoodPrivyLogin } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-privy';

const login = createRobinhoodPrivyLogin(provider, {
  generateSiweMessage,
  loginWithSiwe,
  logout,
});

// A separate, explicitly labeled sign-in button, after provider.connect():
await login.login();
```

Keep the controller stable across renders and forward current hook methods, as shown in the [React example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/privy/README.md). Do not call `login()` from render, restoration, an account-change effect, or a generic Connect button. Login requests `personal_sign`; basic connection does not.

## Lifecycle and limits

The helper uses the current checksummed account and CAIP-2 chain ID to request a Privy-generated message, asks the connected provider to sign it, then submits it to Privy. It never requests accounts itself. It rejects concurrent login calls and removes its provider event listeners when an operation finishes or is invalidated. Account/chain changes, disconnect, `cancel()` or `destroy()` invalidate a pending flow before its next step. Wait for the old operation to settle before retrying from another explicit user action.

Cancellation cannot dismiss an existing wallet prompt or withdraw an already-submitted authentication request. If Privy completes a submitted request after cancellation or a connection change, the helper calls the supplied `logout()` before rejecting. Do not start an unrelated authentication flow while this controller is pending: that cleanup could sign it out too. Handle a failed logout as an authentication cleanup failure. The helper never logs or persists messages, signatures or user data.

`provider.disconnect()` and Privy's `logout()` are separate operations. Signing out does not revoke wallet approval, and disconnecting after a completed login does not automatically invalidate an application authentication session. Apply your application's session policy explicitly. `destroy()` invalidates this helper; dispose the provider separately when the application shuts down.

The [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) distinguishes type/build/SSR and synthetic callback checks from live Privy authentication. Automated browser checks never request a signature. Privy wallet-list integration, embedded wallets, linked accounts, actual login/signatures, and physical wallet behavior are not certified by this helper.

---

# Vanilla browser example

Build the packages at the repository root first with `npm ci && npm run build`.
Then run `npm install` and `npm run dev` in this directory. Copy `.env.example`
to `.env.local`, set your public WalletConnect project ID, allow the actual
example origin in your WalletConnect project, and restart the server.

`index.html` uses the real SDK and WalletConnect relay. It requests account
access only after the Connect button; it never requests a signature or transaction.
This minimal example requires another explicit connection after reload. Passive
restoration with `provider.isAuthorized()` is demonstrated in the ethers and viem examples.

`fixture.html` uses the same SDK dialog with an explicitly synthetic transport.
Its inert QR cannot pair any wallet. It is useful for responsive presentation,
keyboard cancellation, focus restoration, and repeatable screenshots. It is
not a physical-wallet or network compatibility test.

# Source: examples/appkit/README.md

Source URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/README.md

# Robinhood Wallet with Reown AppKit

Use the existing `@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi` connector through AppKit's public `WagmiAdapter`. The AppKit chooser lists Robinhood; the core SDK owns its remote pairing dialog and session. No additional SDK adapter package is required.

Baseline: `@reown/appkit` and `@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi` **1.8.24**, `wagmi` **3.7.7**, `@wagmi/core` **3.6.5**, `viem` **2.57.7**, React **19.3.1**. This example covers AppKit's React + wagmi integration; it does not establish compatibility with AppKit's ethers adapter, other framework bindings, wagmi v2 or non-EVM adapters.

AppKit's broad optional `@wagmi/connectors` range can resolve to a release requiring wagmi core v3. This baseline uses wagmi v3 throughout; a fresh install with wagmi v2 failed on the upstream `@wagmi/core/tempo` export and is not claimed as supported.

## Run the example

From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
cd examples/appkit
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local
# Set VITE_WC_PROJECT_ID, allow this origin in the project settings, then:
npm run dev
```

For a separate application, install the unpublished SDK tarballs together using the [installation guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/README.md#install-from-this-repository). The `file:` dependencies here are for development from this checkout, not npm registry releases.

## Integration

```ts
import { createAppKit } from '@reown/appkit/react';
import { WagmiAdapter } from '@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi';
import { mainnet } from '@reown/appkit/networks';
import { robinhoodWallet } from '@vexi/robinhood-wallet-wagmi';

const projectId = 'YOUR_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID';
const metadata = { name: 'My app', description: 'My app description', url: 'https://my-app.example', icons: [] };
const adapter = new WagmiAdapter({
  projectId,
  networks: [mainnet],
  connectors: [robinhoodWallet({ projectId, metadata })],
  ssr: true,
});
// Initialize once in the browser's application entry point.
const modal = createAppKit({
  adapters: [adapter], networks: [mainnet], projectId, metadata,
  features: { analytics: false, email: false, socials: false, swaps: false, onramp: false },
});
// From an explicit user action:
async function openWalletChooser() { await modal.open(); }
```

Wrap the application in `WagmiProvider` with **`adapter.wagmiConfig`** and `QueryClientProvider`. Do not create a second wagmi config for AppKit. Keep existing custom connectors in the adapter's `connectors` array. AppKit supplies its ordinary wallet entries; this integration does not rename them. The [configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/src/config.ts) and [React app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/examples/appkit/src/main.tsx) show the complete wiring.

The SDK connector retains its own `robinhood` ID and `robinhoodWallet` type. AppKit maps it to an external connector. A `customWallets` catalog entry alone would not install this transport or lifecycle implementation. Leave `showModal` enabled and do not add another QR handler for the Robinhood connector.

Close or Escape in the SDK dialog cancels pairing; retry from AppKit after the previous request settles. Use wagmi's account state and disconnect/reconnect flows. Cancellation cannot dismiss a separate injected wallet permission prompt; it prevents late completion from adopting that connection. Explicit metadata keeps SDK configuration safe during SSR; the Vite app's `window.location.origin` and `createAppKit` setup belong at the browser boundary in an SSR application.

Upstream references: [AppKit React setup](https://docs.reown.com/appkit/react/core/installation), [AppKit options](https://docs.reown.com/appkit/react/core/options), and the tested [WagmiAdapter source](https://github.com/reown-com/appkit/blob/v1.8.24/packages/adapters/wagmi/src/client.ts).

## Verification boundary

Run `node scripts/framework-matrix.mjs appkit` from the repository root to install packed SDK tarballs with the exact dependencies in this example, compile its public types, build it and run synthetic lifecycle checks. See the [verification record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vexi-v1/robinhood-wallet-connector/main/docs/verification.md) for completed results. Do not infer support for other versions, frameworks, networks or physical wallets.

Connection does not request a signature or send a transaction. Real iOS/Android pairing, handoff and signing remain unverified. Keep pairing material and account information out of logs, screenshots and analytics. This is a community integration, not an official Robinhood SDK or endorsement.
